label: rare: first copy output after <DEL> in short sequences starting with 1/n/m (weak)
predicate: (recall_idx == 1) & (L <= 4) & isin(first_tok, [tok("1"), tok("n"), tok("m"), tok("z"), tok("a"), tok("k")])
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps). About 57% of activation mass sits at the step right after <DEL> (input = orig(0), outputting orig(1)), concentrated in short sequences (L=3-4) whose first token is 1, n, or m and whose second token is often z/t/j. The remaining ~36% is in the late original phase (t=3-6), mostly after a g/t/e/j two steps back, again in sequences starting with 1/n/m. No step-level predicate reaches useful precision: even the step after <DEL> with L<=4 fires <1% of the time, and narrowing to first token 1/n/m plus second token z only gets precision 0.38 at recall 0.08. It looks like an idiosyncratic hidden-state conjunction. Magnitude is narrow (median 0.12, max 0.22) and I found nothing that clearly modulates it. Never fires at t<3, after t=10, or at recall_idx>=2.
